name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; US alone opposed a UN test-ban resolution; IAEA flags Iran on 13 Nov
state: New START expired on 5 Feb with no replacement, and the US was the only state to vote against a UN First Committee resolution on the test-ban treaty's entry into force, while saying it keeps a zero-yield testing moratorium (Arms Control Association, 6 Nov). An IAEA report on 13 Nov says it cannot confirm Iran has not diverted nuclear material (The National). No nuclear test, change in alert levels or threatened use was found as of 15 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: There is no change to public safety advice. Arms-control lapses tend to raise the risk of miscalculation over years rather than days; the UK government publishes emergency preparedness guidance online.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired 5 Feb)

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
